newsitem.title: CANADA: AEC, North Dakota Indians sign oil deal.
newsitem.headline: AEC, North Dakota Indians sign oil deal.

text.p: Alberta Energy Co Ltd said on Thursday it signed an oil exploration and production agreement with three Indian tribes in North Dakota.
It is the second such deal in the last three months between American Indians in northern states and Canadian oil companies.

AEC said its subsidiary, Alenco Oil & Gas (N.D) Inc, signed the exploration deal with the three affiliated tribes that form the Fort Berthold Indian Reservation, located 85 miles southeast of Williston, North Dakota.
The tribes include the Mandan, Hidatsa and Arikara.
Under the agreement, Alenco would obtain a 100 percent working interest in the petroleum and natural gas rights on up to 459,000 acres of tribal and allotted lands on the reservation, AEC said.
In December, Gulf Canada Resources Ltd signed an agreement with the Sioux and Assiniboine tribes of Fort Peck, Montana giving it access to 110,000 acres of new exploration lands in that state.
AEC said the lands covered by the agreement were similar in size to its block at Suffield in southeast Alberta, a main operating area for the company.

"By partnering with the Three Affiliated Tribes, we are able to achieve our objective of maintaining high working interests in hydrocarbon-prone areas," AEC chief executive Gwyn Morgan said in a statement.
Tribal council chairman Russell Mason said the deal was the largest undertaken on the reservation, which has seen little exploration by oil companies to date.
